title: Harrow: Synthesis of Optical Logic Circuits via Harmonic Mean and Integer Partition
problem: Photonic integrated circuits suffer from signal attenuation along light propagation paths, requiring optical-electrical conversions that introduce unwanted delays and inefficiency.
motivation: PICs offer energy-efficient computation over CMOS, but signal attenuation during optical logic synthesis limits practical implementations.
method: Harrow designs optical logic circuits starting with a binary decision diagram (a tree-like representation of logic operations) and then optimizes optical combiners—devices that merge light signals. It improves how efficiently these combiners preserve signal strength using harmonic mean optimization (a mathematical method that finds the best balance between multiple objectives). It also removes redundant combiners using integer partition (a technique for systematically grouping components to identify and eliminate duplicates). Finally, it arranges these optimizations in a sequence that produces the best overall circuit performance.
key_novelty: Harrow combines harmonic mean optimization of DC combiners (devices that merge light signals) with integer partition-based redundancy elimination to improve signal efficiency in optical logic circuits.
contributions: Harmonic mean optimization of DC combiners to improve signal efficiency factor
Integer partition method to eliminate redundant optical combiners
Optimized operational sequence for combining techniques
Outperforms state-of-the-art in terms of efficiency factor
limitations: Specific efficiency metrics and performance numbers not disclosed in abstract; scalability to larger circuits not discussed.
